name: Yeh'kinya
summary: Yeh'kinya is a jungle troll scholar residing at Steamwheedle Port on the desert coast of Tanaris. Claiming to seek ancient lore and artifacts to understand dark powers, he dispatches willing adventurers across Azeroth on missions to gather lost troll relics.

sections.title: The Scholar at Steamwheedle Port
sections.body: Lounging among the goblins and dockworkers of Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya presents himself as a quiet student of history and spirits. He recruits travelers to track down obscure magical items across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, from ancient eggs in the Hinterlands to stone prophecy tablets buried in the ruins of Zul'Farrak. While he claims these errands serve peaceful academic inquiry into ancient troll history, his specific focus on the blood god Hakkar draws suspicion from watchful onlookers.

sections.title: The Serpent's Deceit
sections.body: Beneath his scholarly guise, Yeh'kinya is a fanatical worshipper of Hakkar the Soulflayer. Every artifact and soul essence he gathers is carefully manipulated to prepare for the dread Blood God's physical rebirth into Azeroth. Once his plot is pieced together and exposed by Prospector Ironboot, Yeh'kinya sheds all pretense of friendship. Rather than answering for his treason, he transforms into a green wind serpent and flees across the open sea toward the south seas, leaving duped heroes to seek aid from the Zandalari on Yojamba Isle.

faq.answer: Yeh'kinya is a jungle troll found standing near the water at Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris. He presents himself as a scholar seeking historical relics and spirits, with a particular interest in the troll god Hakkar.

faq.q: Why does Yeh'kinya want the Prophecy of Mosh'aru and the Ancient Egg?
faq.answer: Yeh'kinya says he needs these artifacts for his study of ancient troll history and spirits. The Mosh'aru tablets lie in the ruins of Zul'Farrak and the Ancient Egg in the Hinterlands, and both tie into his interest in Hakkar.

angles.text: Darkspear trolls recognize the mortal peril of Hakkar's resurgence.
Priests sensitive to spiritual essence may find Yeh'kinya's casual collection of trapped screecher spirits deeply troubling.
